analysis:
Examined the MediaIngest.swift patch, the docs/threat-model.yaml change and the libs/mlx-swift-lm submodule bump.

MediaIngest.swift (~769-801): inline video data-URI header admission goes from two case-insensitive comparisons to a lowercased Set lookup. It adds data:video/x-m4v;base64 and data:video/mov;base64, both of which are MP4 or QuickTime labels. The check still requires a base64 data: header. http(s) and file URIs are still rejected, because the header must match the exact set. dataFromDataURI still applies maxMediaDecodedBytes. The diff does not touch the downstream duration, frame-pixel, count and aggregate caps. The change is label-only and relies on MemoryBackedVideoAsset sniffing the container from the bytes (per the code comment). The memory-backed path with AVURLAssetReferenceRestrictions.forbidAll is unchanged, so T-050's no-plaintext-file mitigation still holds, and new MIME labels do not add a file-writing path. The extra accepted labels slightly widen the AVFoundation parser input surface, but it is the same MP4/QuickTime parser already reachable via mp4/quicktime. No new finding. The threat-model text update at yaml line 1969-1970 matches the code (x-m4v, mov, quicktime, mp4).

The threat-model yaml units shown (T-041 tail through T-058, lines 1395-2261) are context. The only changed hunk is the T-050 mitigation wording; no mitigation statuses were weakened.

Submodule libs/mlx-swift-lm bumps from 7bed8216 to 54227bab. The submodule contents are not supplied, so I cannot verify that MemoryBackedVideoAsset/UserInput changes (referenced by T-050 as libs/mlx-swift-lm/Libraries/MLXLMCommon/MemoryBackedVideoAsset.swift) still preserve the memory-only, forbidAll-restricted, range-bounded loader. They may also be what makes container sniffing accept mov/x-m4v. That is an unverified contract, so I recommend deeper review of the submodule diff. Remaining integration question: confirm the submodule update does not introduce a file-URL fallback, a network fetch, or an A-001 plaintext exposure.
